newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds weak across the curve, focus on EBR.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds weak across the curve, focus on EBR.

text.p: Irish government bonds were weaker across the curve, more at the front-end than in longer paper, in thin late trade on Tuesday, dealers said.
Dealers said the market awaited the release of end-January Exchequer Borrowing Requirement data at 1630 GMT.
"We're waiting on the EBR data. It is expected to show buoyancy in the Irish economy," one dealer said.

"The Irish market is just paddling along in narrow ranges. We've seen selling at the front-end but overall we've performed quite well. The feeling is that Germany is approaching resistance levels," the dealer added.

By 1600 GMT, the key benchmark eight percent bond due 2006 was down five pence from Monday's close at 109.50 to yield 6.51 percent while the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 had eased 25 pence from the close at 102.25 to yield 5.84 percent.
Dealers said Irish bonds were trading at 94 basis points over German bunds in the 10-year area and 149 basis points over bunds in the five-year area.
No rate change was expected in the U.S. at the end of the two-day meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee, which got under way on Tuesday, dealers said.
